claim: Partial/complete pathologic response following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in pancreatic cancer (PDAC) patients undergoing pancreatectomy is associated with improved survival.
source: Partial/complete pathologic response following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in pancreatic cancer (PDAC) patients undergoing pancreatectomy is associated with improved survival.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work from the authors' group (Macedo et al., 2019) as stated in the Introduction section.

claim: 94 PDAC patients underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy and pancreatectomy between July 2015 and December 2019.
source: Patients with localized PDAC who received NAC with either mFOLFIRINOX, gemcitabine/abraxane, or both and underwent pancreatectomy between July 2015 and December 2019 at a tertiary academic center (n=101) were enrolled.
evidence: The manuscript describes the clinical cohort with specific dates and patient numbers.

claim: Patients received a median of 4 months of neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
source: Patients received a median of 4 months of NAC (range 2–14)
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the patient cohort reported in the Results section.

claim: 70% of patients achieved partial/complete pathologic response following neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
source: Following NAC, partial/complete PR was achieved in 70% (66/94) while 28 patients (30%) demonstrated poor/absent PR
evidence: This is a direct calculation from the patient cohort data presented in the Results section.

claim: Pre-chemotherapy absolute NLR was significantly lower in patients with partial/complete pathologic response compared with poor/absent pathologic response (2.53 vs 3.97; p<0.001).
source: Median pre-NAC aNLR was significantly lower in patients with partial/complete PR compared with poor/absent PR (2.53 vs 3.97; p<0.001) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of patient data and visualization in Figure 1B.

claim: A net attenuation in ΔNLR was observed in patients demonstrating partial/complete pathologic response compared with a net increase in ΔNLR in poor/absent pathologic response (median –0.38 vs. +0.21; p=0.01).
source: Moreover, a net attenuation in ΔNLR was observed in patients demonstrating partial/complete PR compared with a net increase in ΔNLR in poor/absent PR (median –0.38 vs. +0.21; p=0.01 respectively; Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of patient data and visualization in Figure 1C.

claim: Higher pre-chemotherapy NLR is independently associated with poor/absent pathologic response (OR 0.02, 95% CI 0.003–0.15; p<0.001).
source: On multivariable modeling, higher aNLR (OR 0.02, 95% CI 0.003–0.15; p<0.001 [Ref: low aNLR])
evidence: This claim is supported by multivariable logistic regression analysis presented in the Results section.

claim: Higher ΔNLR is independently associated with poor/absent pathologic response (OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01–0.33; p=0.002).
source: higher ΔNLR (OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01–0.33; p=0.002 [Ref: low ΔNLR])
evidence: This claim is supported by multivariable logistic regression analysis presented in the Results section.

claim: Any percent decline in CA19-9 during neoadjuvant chemotherapy is independently associated with partial/complete pathologic response (OR 1.82, 95% CI 0.001–3.74; p=0.05).
source: any %decline in CA19-9 during NAC (OR 1.82, 95% CI 0.001–3.74; p=0.05 [Ref: any %increase in CA19-9])
evidence: This claim is supported by multivariable logistic regression analysis presented in the Results section.

claim: A combined NLR model encompassing both aNLR and ΔNLR most efficiently predicted pathologic response with an AUC of 0.96.
source: Bootstrap-validated AUC-derived analysis revealed that a combined NLR model encompassing both aNLR and ΔNLR most efficiently predicted PR with an AUC of 0.96 (Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by bootstrap-validated AUC analysis presented in the Results section.

claim: Patients with an NLR score ≤0 demonstrated improved disease-free survival compared with patients with an NLR score >0 (median 1.4 vs 0.7 years; p=0.006).
source: Patients with an NLR score ≤0 demonstrated improved DFS (median 1.4 vs 0.7 years; p=0.006)
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis presented in the Results section.

claim: Patients with an NLR score ≤0 demonstrated improved overall survival compared with patients with an NLR score >0 (median 3.6 vs 2.1 years; p=0.002).
source: OS (median 3.6 vs 2.1 years; p=0.002) compared with patients with an NLR score >0 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis presented in the Results section and visualized in Figure 1E.

claim: Treatment with 25 μg anti-Ly6G dosing achieved approximately 50% attenuation in circulating Ly6G+:CD3+ NLR ratio in orthotopic KPC tumor-bearing mice compared with vehicle treatment.
source: treatment of orthotopic KPC tumor-bearing mice with neutrophil-attenuating 25 μg anti-Ly6G dosing achieved approximately 50% attenuation in circulating Ly6G+:CD3+ NLR ratio compared with vehicle treatment (Appendix 1—figure 3A)
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments presented in the Results section.

claim: Treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel did not significantly decrease Ly6G+:CD3+ ratios in orthotopic KPC tumor-bearing mice.
source: treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel, however, did not significantly decrease Ly6G+:CD3+ ratios (Appendix 1—figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments presented in the Results section.

claim: Concurrent treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G significantly decreased pancreatic tumor weight compared to gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone in orthotopic KPC tumor-bearing mice.
source: While gemcitabine/paclitaxel treatment expectedly decreased PDAC tumor size compared with vehicle and anti-Ly6G alone treatments, concurrent treatment of tumor-bearing mice with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G further significantly decreased pancreatic tumor weight (Figure 2A)
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor weight measurements from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Concurrent treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G significantly decreased metastatic outgrowth in orthotopic KPC tumor-bearing mice.
source: concurrent treatment of tumor-bearing mice with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G further significantly decreased pancreatic tumor weight (Figure 2A) and metastatic outgrowth, graded by the presence of tumor deposits at six extra-pancreatic sites (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by metastatic burden assessment from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mice treated with combination gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G treatment did not incur additional systemic toxicity during treatment as measured by mouse weights and systemic ALT levels.
source: Importantly, mice treated with combination gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G treatment did not incur additional systemic toxicity during treatment as measured by mouse weights (Appendix 1—figure 4A) and systemic ALT levels (Appendix 1—figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by toxicity measurements from preclinical experiments presented in the Results section.

claim: NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G improved chemosensitivity as evidenced by significantly decreased tumor area by H&E staining (p=0.01) compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone.
source: Compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G improved chemosensitivity as evidenced by significantly decreased tumor area by H&E staining (p=0.01; Figure 2C)
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G increased cleaved caspase-3 in gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G treated mice compared with all other treatment groups.
source: as well as increased cleaved caspase-3 and microvessel (CD31) density (Figure 2D) in gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G treated mice compared with all other treatment groups.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G increased microvessel (CD31) density in gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G treated mice compared with all other treatment groups.
source: as well as increased cleaved caspase-3 and microvessel (CD31) density (Figure 2D) in gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G treated mice compared with all other treatment groups.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In PKT genetically engineered mice, NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G improved chemosensitivity versus chemotherapy alone as evidenced by decreased primary tumor weights (p=0.004).
source: In this model as well, NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G improved chemosensitivity vs. chemotherapy alone as evidenced by decreased primary tumor weights (p=004; Figure 2E)
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor weight measurements from PKT mouse experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: In PKT genetically engineered mice, NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G improved chemosensitivity versus chemotherapy alone as evidenced by decreased tumor area by H&E staining (p=0.008).
source: and tumor area by H&E staining (P=0.008; Figure 2F) at endpoint analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis from PKT mouse experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claim: NLR attenuation significantly reduced circulating Ly6G+Ly6CdimF4/80- neutrophilic cells in tumor-bearing animals.
source: In tumor-bearing animals, NLR attenuation significantly reduced—but did not abolish—circulating Ly6G+Ly6CdimF4/80- neutrophilic cells
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments presented in the Results section.

claim: NLR attenuation resulted in a compensatory increase in Ly6ChiLy6G-F4/80- monocytic cells via flow cytometry from splenocyte-derived CD11b+ cells.
source: although a compensatory increase in Ly6ChiLy6G-F4/80- monocytic cells was observed via flow cytometry from splenocyte-derived CD11b+ cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: NLR attenuation—either alone or in combination with gemcitabine/paclitaxel—significantly decreased tumor-infiltrating Ly6G/Gr1+ neutrophilic myeloid derived suppressor cells in the PDAC tumor microenvironment.
source: As expected, NLR attenuation—either alone or in combination with gemcitabine/paclitaxel—significantly decreased tumor-infiltrating Ly6G/Gr1+ neutrophilic myeloid derived suppressor cells in the PDAC TME (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G significantly increased infiltration of both intratumoral CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle arms.
source: Flow cytometric analysis revealed that treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G significantly increased infiltration of both intratumoral CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells, as well as augmented antigen experience (PD-1+) and degranulating capacity (CD107a+) specifically in the CD8+ T-cell compartment (Figure 3C), compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle arms.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G augmented antigen experience (PD-1+) specifically in the CD8+ T-cell compartment compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle arms.
source: Flow cytometric analysis revealed that treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G significantly increased infiltration of both intratumoral CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells, as well as augmented antigen experience (PD-1+) and degranulating capacity (CD107a+) specifically in the CD8+ T-cell compartment (Figure 3C), compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle arms.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G augmented degranulating capacity (CD107a+) specifically in the CD8+ T-cell compartment compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle arms.
source: Flow cytometric analysis revealed that treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G significantly increased infiltration of both intratumoral CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells, as well as augmented antigen experience (PD-1+) and degranulating capacity (CD107a+) specifically in the CD8+ T-cell compartment (Figure 3C), compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle arms.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Increased infiltration in both CD4+ and CD8+ central memory (CD44+CD62L+CD103-) T-cells were observed in gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G-treated tumors compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle-treated tumors.
source: Interestingly, increased infiltration in both CD4+ and CD8+ central memory (CD44+CD62L+CD103-), but not effector (CD44+CD62L-) or tissue-resident memory (CD44+CD62L-CD103+), T-cells were observed in gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G-treated tumors compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, anti-Ly6G alone, or vehicle-treated tumors (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: CAF-derived IL-6 engages in tumor-permissive crosstalk by activating STAT3 signaling within tumor cells.
source: Furthermore, prior work from our group has revealed that CAF-derived IL-6 engages in tumor-permissive crosstalk by activating STAT3 signaling within tumor cells (Nagathihalli et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work from the authors' group.

claim: Heightened CAF-tumor cell IL-6/STAT-3 signaling crosstalk is a central mediator of chemoresistance in PDAC.
source: and that heightened CAF-tumor cell IL-6/STAT-3 signaling crosstalk is a central mediator of chemoresistance in PDAC (Dosch et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Concurrent treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G (p=0.006)—but not anti-Ly6G alone (p=0.12) or gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone (p=0.49)—significantly reduced iCAF:myCAF cellular ratios in vivo compared with vehicle treatment.
source: Compared with vehicle treatment, concurrent treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G (P=0.006)—but not anti-Ly6G alone (p=0.12) or gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone (p=0.49) treatment—significantly reduced iCAF (CD45-CD31-PDPN+Ly6C+ MHCII-):myofibroblastic CAF (myCAF; CD45-CD31-PDPN+Ly6C-MHCII-) cellular ratios in vivo (Figure 4A; Appendix 1—figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PDPN is near-exclusively expressed in human and murine PDAC-associated CAFs via scRNAseq.
source: Furthermore, leveraging the near-exclusive expression of PDPN/Pdpn in human and murine PDAC-associated CAFs via scRNAseq (Datta et al., 2022; Steele et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior scRNAseq studies.

claim: Significant reduction in co-expressing PDPN+CXCL1+ stromal cells was observed in tumors from PKT genetically engineered mice treated with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone (p=0.02).
source: we observed significant reduction in co-expressing PDPN+CXCL1+ stromal cells—presumed iCAFs—in tumors from PKT genetically engineered mice treated with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G compared with gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone (p=0.02; Figure 4B)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from PKT mouse experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Pre-treatment tumors from PDAC patients who demonstrated poor/absent pathologic response had significantly higher ratio of CD11b+CD15+ to CD3+CD8+ cells (NLR; normalized to 5000 total single cells) compared with partial/complete response (15.8±2.8 vs 7.4±3.9; p=0.039).
source: Image segmentation and quantification revealed significantly higher ratio of CD11b+CD15+ to CD3+CD8+ cells (NLR; normalized to 5000 total single cells) in pre-treatment tumors from PDAC patients who demonstrated poor/absent pathologic response compared with partial/complete response (15.8±2.8 vs 7.4±3.9; p=0.039) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging mass cytometry data from human PDAC specimens shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Increased NLR in patients with poor/absent pathologic response correlated with significantly higher mean intensity of α-SMA expression (41.9±26.6 vs 18.4±16.6 pixels/cell; p<0.001) in cancer associated fibroblasts.
source: Interestingly, increased NLR in patients with poor/absent pathologic response correlated with significantly higher mean intensity of α-SMA expression (41.9±26.6 vs 18.4±16.6 pixels/cell; p<0.001) in—but not absolute density of—cancer associated fibroblasts in tumor ROIs (Figure 4D)
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging mass cytometry data from human PDAC specimens shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Increased NLR in patients with poor/absent pathologic response correlated with relative abundance of co-expressed PDPN+CXCL1+ iCAF populations (29.7 ± 8.8% vs 18.4 ± 7.4% tumor area; p<0.001).
source: as well as relative abundance of co-expressed PDPN+CXCL1+ iCAF populations in corresponding tumor sections (29.7 ± 8.8% vs 18.4 ± 7.4% tumor area; p<0.001; Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from human PDAC specimens shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G (p=0.0002), but not anti-Ly6G alone (p=0.06) or gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone (p=0.08), resulted in decreased intratumoral IL-6 levels compared to vehicle treatment.
source: The reprogramming of iCAF polarization following NLR attenuation during chemotherapy in the preclinical models was reflected in decreased intratumoral IL-6 and CXCL-1 (data not shown) levels following treatment with gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G (p=0.0002), but not anti-Ly6G alone (p=0.06) or gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone (p=0.08) treatment, compared to vehicle treatment (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Compared with vehicle, anti-Ly6G alone, or gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, gemcitabine/paclitaxel plus anti-Ly6G treatment resulted in significantly lower pSTAT3 expression in the tumor cell/epithelial compartment in vivo (p<0.01).
source: In parallel with these findings, compared with vehicle, anti-Ly6G alone, or gemcitabine/paclitaxel alone, gemcitabine/paclitaxel +anti-Ly6G treatment resulted in significantly lower pSTAT3 expression in the tumor cell/epithelial compartment in vivo (p<0.01; Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 4G.

claim: IL-1β is the most robustly secreted cytokine from tumor-infiltrating Ly6G+F4/80- neutrophils isolated from orthotopic KPC tumors.
source: To explore a mechanistic link between tumor-infiltrating neutrophils and iCAF-mediated IL-6/STAT-3 signaling in the PDAC TME, we characterized the secretome of tumor-infiltrating Ly6G+F4/80- neutrophils isolated from orthotopic KPC tumors, revealing IL-1β as the most robustly secreted cytokine (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplex cytokine array data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Systemic NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G treatment—with or without chemotherapy—resulted in significant diminution of IL-1β secretion in tumor lysates compared with vehicle or chemotherapy treatment in vivo (ANOVA p<0.001).
source: Systemic NLR attenuation with anti-Ly6G treatment—with or without chemotherapy—resulted in significant diminution of IL-1β secretion in tumor lysates compared with vehicle or chemotherapy treatment in vivo (ANOVA p<0.001; Figure 5B)
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from preclinical experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Ex vivo co-cultures of KPC CAFs with tumor-infiltrating Ly6G+F4/80- neutrophils induced a nearly 20-fold increase in CAF-intrinsic Il6 transcription (p<0.0001), which was significantly abrogated by either neutralization of IL-1β (p<0.0001) or by pre-incubation of CAFs with IL-1R1 inhibitor Anakinra (p<0.0001).
source: Ex vivo co-cultures of KPC CAFs with tumor-infiltrating Ly6G+F4/80- neutrophils derived from orthotopic tumor-bearing KPC mice induced a nearly 20-fold increase in CAF-intrinsic Il6 transcription (p<0.0001), which was significantly abrogated by either neutralization of IL-1β (p<0.0001) or by pre-incubation of CAFs with IL-1R1 inhibitor Anakinra (Nagathihalli et al., 2016; p<0.0001; Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data from ex vivo co-culture experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: IL-6 secretion from CAF-neutrophil co-cultures was dramatically increased and significantly rescued with either IL-1β or IL-1R1 inhibition (all p<0.0001).
source: These results were validated by IL-6 ELISA, which demonstrated a dramatic increase in IL-6 secretion from CAF-neutrophil co-cultures, and was significantly rescued with either IL-1β or IL-1R1 inhibition (all p<0.0001; Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from ex vivo co-culture experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cxcl1 transcription in CAFs was induced nearly 22-fold following co-culture with tumor-infiltrating neutrophils, and significantly abrogated with either IL-1β or IL-1R1 inhibition (all p<0.0001).
source: Cxcl1 transcription in CAFs—another key iCAF marker—was similarly induced nearly 22-fold following co-culture with tumor-infiltrating neutrophils, and significantly abrogated with either IL-1β or IL-1R1 inhibition (all p<0.0001; Appendix 1—figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data from ex vivo co-culture experiments referenced in the Results section.

claim: KPC tumor cells demonstrated significantly higher pSTAT3 expression when incubated with conditioned media from intratumoral neutrophil-CAF co-cultures alone compared with conditioned media from neutrophil-CAF co-cultures treated with either anti-IL-1β or anti-IL-6 neutralizing antibodies.
source: Finally, KPC tumor cells demonstrated significantly higher pSTAT3 expression when incubated with conditioned media (CM) from intratumoral neutrophil-CAF co-cultures alone compared with CM from neutrophil-CAF co-cultures treated with either anti-IL-1β or anti-IL-6 neutralizing antibodies (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data from ex vivo experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Neutrophil-derived IL-1β plays a role in promoting iCAF polarization and inducing CAF-tumor cell IL-6/STAT3 signaling in the PDAC tumor microenvironment.
source: Together, these data reveal a role for neutrophil-derived IL-1β in promoting iCAF polarization and inducing CAF-tumor cell IL-6/STAT3 signaling in the PDAC TME, which is a central mediator of chemoresistance (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the collective experimental data presented in Figure 5 and discussed in the Results section.

claim: Major pathologic response following neoadjuvant chemotherapy is associated with improved overall survival in patients with operable pancreatic cancer.
source: Our group has previously reported that major pathologic response following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is associated with improved overall survival (Macedo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work from the authors' group.

claim: NLR has emerged as a promising biomarker in localized and advanced PDAC.
source: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) has emerged as a promising biomarker in localized and advanced PDAC.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge and citations in the Introduction section.

claim: NLR has prognostic value in advanced unresectable PDAC.
source: Beyond its prognostic value in advanced unresectable disease (Iwai et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Pre-surgery NLR has value in forecasting recurrence in patients undergoing upfront pancreatectomy.
source: recent evidence implicates the value of pre-surgery NLR in forecasting recurrence in patients undergoing upfront pancreatectomy (Nywening et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Pre- and post-treatment NLR predict pathologic response following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in PDAC.
source: as well as pre- and post-treatment NLR in predicting pathologic response following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (Hasegawa et al., 2016; Kubo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The precise relationship between NLR dynamics during neoadjuvant treatment and pathologic response and/or survival in localized PDAC patients undergoing pancreatectomy has not been previously explored.
source: However, the precise relationship between NLR dynamics during neoadjuvant treatment and pathologic response and/or survival in localized PDAC patients undergoing pancreatectomy has not been previously explored.
evidence: This claim represents a gap in knowledge identified by the authors.

claim: Stromal inflammation in the PDAC tumor microenvironment—predominantly through inflammatory polarization of cancer-associated fibroblasts (iCAF) and CAF-derived secretion of IL-6—is a major driver of chemoresistance in PDAC.
source: Emerging evidence implicates stromal inflammation in the PDAC tumor microenvironment (TME)—predominantly through inflammatory polarization of cancer-associated fibroblasts (iCAF) and CAF-derived secretion of IL-6 (Öhlund et al., 2017)—as a major driver of chemoresistance in PDAC (Hosein et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Modern multi-agent chemotherapy delivered in the neoadjuvant setting for localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is an increasingly popular treatment sequencing strategy.
source: Modern multi-agent chemotherapy delivered in the neoadjuvant setting for localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an increasingly popular treatment sequencing strategy (Datta and Merchant, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: 78% of the study cohort had borderline resectable or locally advanced disease.
source: Of 94 eligible patients (mean age 67, 58% female, 6% with germline homologous recombination deficiency genotype [BRCA2, n=5; PALB2, n=1]), 78% had borderline resectable or locally advanced disease.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the patient cohort reported in the Results section.

claim: 52% of patients received mFOLFIRINOX chemotherapy.
source: Patients received a median of 4 months of NAC (range 2–14), 52% received mFOLFIRINOX
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the patient cohort reported in the Results section.

claim: 6% of patients received neoadjuvant radiotherapy.
source: and a minority of patients (6%) received neoadjuvant radiotherapy.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the patient cohort reported in the Results section.

claim: Median aNLR or ΔNLR did not differ significantly between patients who received neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX vs. gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel.
source: Of note, median aNLR or ΔNLR did not differ significantly between patients who received neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX vs. gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel (3.00 vs 3.09, p=0.47; –0.02 to –0.25, p=0.16).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison from the patient cohort reported in the Results section.

claim: NAC duration, BMI, resectability status, and use of neoadjuvant radiotherapy were not independent predictors of achieving partial/complete pathologic response following NAC.
source: On multivariable modeling, higher aNLR (OR 0.02, 95% CI 0.003–0.15; p<0.001 [Ref: low aNLR]), higher ΔNLR (OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01–0.33; p=0.002 [Ref: low ΔNLR]), and any %decline in CA19-9 during NAC (OR 1.82, 95% CI 0.001–3.74; p=0.05 [Ref: any %increase in CA19-9])—but not NAC duration, BMI, resectability status, or use of neoadjuvant radiotherapy—were independent predictors of achieving partial/complete PR following NAC (Figure 1D, Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: This is a result from multivariable logistic regression analysis presented in the Results section.

claim: At a median follow-up of 30 (IQR 7–49) months, 2 year and 5 year survival in this selected cohort of patients undergoing resection were 59% and 34%, respectively.
source: At a median follow-up of 30 (IQR 7–49) months, 2 year and 5 year survival in this selected cohort of patients undergoing resection were 59% and 34%, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the patient cohort reported in the Results section.

claim: Systemic chemotherapy does not appear to impact tumor-infiltrating neutrophils in preclinical studies.
source: Notwithstanding, since systemic chemotherapy does not appear to impact tumor-infiltrating neutrophils (Nywening et al., 2018) or circulating NLR in our preclinical studies
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and data from the authors' preclinical studies.

claim: Systemic chemotherapy does not appear to impact circulating NLR in preclinical studies.
source: Notwithstanding, since systemic chemotherapy does not appear to impact tumor-infiltrating neutrophils (Nywening et al., 2018) or circulating NLR in our preclinical studies
evidence: This claim is supported by data from the authors' preclinical studies.

claim: Therapeutic strategies to attenuate NLR during NAC may improve pathologic response in operable PDAC.
source: these data also suggest that therapeutic strategies to attenuate NLR during NAC may improve pathologic response in operable PDAC.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the study's findings.

claim: Depletion of Ly6G+ neutrophilic myeloid-derived suppressor cells unmasks adaptive immunity.
source: Our data add nuance to previous findings indicating that depletion of Ly6G+ neutrophilic myeloid-derived suppressor cells unmasks adaptive immunity (Stromnes et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Ablation of CXCR2+ tumor-associated neutrophils augments IFN-γ+CD8+ T-cell infiltration to potentiate FOLFIRINOX responses in PDAC models.
source: or that ablation of CXCR2+ tumor-associated neutrophils augments IFN-γ+CD8+ T-cell infiltration to potentiate FOLFIRINOX responses in PDAC models (Nywening et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Systemic neutrophilic silencing drives a compensatory and dynamic myelopoiesis (e.g. of CCR2+ macrophages) that thwarts anti-tumor immunity.
source: Given that systemic neutrophilic silencing is not only clinically impractical, but also drives a compensatory and dynamic myelopoiesis (e.g. of CCR2+ macrophages) that thwarts anti-tumor immunity (Nywening et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Combining chemotherapy with therapeutic strategies to mitigate neutrophil-stromal-tumor cell IL-1β/IL-6/STAT-3 signaling in PDAC patients may be advantageous.
source: As such, the improved chemosensitivity associated with NLR attenuation in our preclinical models suggest that combining chemotherapy with therapeutic strategies to mitigate neutrophil-stromal-tumor cell IL-1β/IL-6/STAT-3 signaling in PDAC patients may be advantageous.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the study's findings.

claim: The Precision PromiseSM trial is investigating anti-IL-1β antagonism in combination with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel and PD-1 inhibition in patients with advanced PDAC (NCT04581343).
source: Results from the Precision PromiseSM trial investigating anti-IL-1β antagonism in combination with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel and PD-1 inhibition in patients with advanced PDAC (NCT04581343) are eagerly awaited.
evidence: This claim references an ongoing clinical trial.

claim: PDPN is widely used as a pan-CAF marker in multiple PDAC-related studies.
